use_case: Fleet-tracking data pipeline: running a retention purge of GPS pings, where a later legal exception protects vehicles with open insurance claims.
situation: The user first set a rule to delete GPS pings older than 90 days. Later they added an exception: vehicles with an open insurance claim must keep all their pings. A query then showed that one fleet-12 vehicle has an open claim. The purge script so far only filters by date, and the dry-run count includes that vehicle.
must_keep: The 90-day purge rule, the later exception that excludes vehicles with an open claim, and the query result showing RTX-4F21 in fleet 12 has an open claim.
may_drop: File listings, the source dump, test and git logs, the stale 180-day staging retention doc, the dry-run count, and chit-chat about cron schedules.
why_judges_fail: The dry-run block shares the most words with the goal ("expurgo", "frota 12") and looks ready to run. A judge may keep it and drop the short user exception or the claim query result, and then approve a purge that destroys evidence the legal team needs.
